Upper chest at the level of the sternal angle (trunk)
questions.explanation: T2 runs at the sternal angle and the apex of the axilla. There is no separate T1 band on the chest on standard maps: below the clavicle the supraclavicular (C3-C4) territory meets T2.

questions.prompt: Chest band between the sternal angle and the nipple line (trunk)

questions.explanation: T4 ≈ nipple level; the fourth intercostal space in the midclavicular line is the more reproducible landmark.

Abdominal band immediately above the umbilicus (trunk)
Lower abdominal band immediately below the umbilicus (trunk)
Lower abdominal band just above the inguinal ligament (trunk)
questions.explanation: This map assigns T12 to the lowest abdominal band above the groin. The T12-L1 boundary differs between maps; standardized sensory testing places the T12 point at the midpoint of the inguinal ligament.

Lateral shoulder over the deltoid, the 'regimental badge' area (anterior view)
Lateral aspect of the upper arm below the deltoid (anterior view)
Lateral forearm from the elbow to the wrist (anterior view)
questions.explanation: Cutaneous branch = lateral cutaneous nerve of forearm (lateral antebrachial cutaneous).

questions.prompt: Medial side of the arm and medial side of the forearm down to the wrist (anterior view)
questions.answer: Medial Cutaneous Nerves of Arm & Forearm
options: Medial Cutaneous Nerves of Arm & Forearm
questions.explanation: Medial arm = medial cutaneous nerve of arm (medial brachial cutaneous, C8-T1); the uppermost medial arm toward the axilla is intercostobrachial (T2). Medial forearm = medial cutaneous nerve of forearm (medial antebrachial cutaneous).

questions.prompt: Medial palm, little finger and medial half of the ring finger (anterior view)
Lateral palm, thumb, index and middle fingers and lateral half of the ring finger (anterior view)
Skin over the top of the shoulder above the spine of the scapula (posterior view)
Lateral shoulder over the deltoid (posterior view)
Posterior arm and forearm, lateral dorsum of the hand and the proximal dorsal thumb, index, middle and lateral half of the ring finger, sparing the fingertips (posterior view)

questions.explanation: Medial cutaneous nerve of forearm = medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve (medial cord of the brachial plexus).
Cutaneous branch = lateral cutaneous nerve of forearm (lateral antebrachial cutaneous).

Dorsal fingertips of the thumb, index and middle fingers and the lateral half of the ring finger (posterior view)

options: Anterior Cutaneous Branches of Femoral Nerve
questions.explanation: Femoral branch of the genitofemoral nerve (L1-L2). The superomedial thigh and groin crease are ilioinguinal (L1), a different nerve.

questions.prompt: Lateral thigh from the hip to the knee (anterior view)
options: Anterior Cutaneous Branches of Femoral Nerve

questions.prompt: Small patch on the medial mid-thigh (anterior view)
options: Anterior Cutaneous Branches of Femoral Nerve
questions.explanation: The obturator nerve's skin patch on the medial thigh is small and variable and may be absent.

questions.prompt: Anterior thigh down to the knee (anterior view)
questions.answer: Anterior Cutaneous Branches of Femoral Nerve
options: Anterior Cutaneous Branches of Femoral Nerve
questions.explanation: Anterior cutaneous branches of the femoral nerve = intermediate and medial cutaneous nerves of thigh.

questions.prompt: Proximal lateral calf, just below the knee (anterior view)
options: Medial Calcaneal Branches of Tibial Nerve

questions.prompt: Medial leg from the knee to the medial ankle (anterior view)
options: Medial Calcaneal Branches of Tibial Nerve

questions.prompt: Distal anterolateral leg and most of the dorsum of the foot, sparing the first web space (anterior view)
options: Medial Calcaneal Branches of Tibial Nerve
questions.explanation: Clinical/older name: superficial peroneal nerve. It supplies most dorsal foot skin; exceptions are the first dorsal web space (deep fibular), the foot margins (sural laterally, saphenous medially) and the distal dorsal toe tips (plantar digital branches).

questions.prompt: Skin of the first dorsal web space, between the great and second toes (anterior view)
options: Medial Calcaneal Branches of Tibial Nerve
questions.explanation: Clinical/older name: deep peroneal nerve. Its cutaneous territory is the first dorsal web space only.

questions.prompt: Lateral border of the foot and lateral side of the little toe (anterior view)
options: Medial Calcaneal Branches of Tibial Nerve
Anterior Cutaneous Branches of Femoral Nerve

questions.prompt: Narrow strip along the medial edge of the thigh to the knee, anteromedial skin seen from behind (posterior view)
questions.answer: Anterior Cutaneous Branches of Femoral Nerve
options: Anterior Cutaneous Branches of Femoral Nerve
questions.explanation: This strip is the medial cutaneous nerve of thigh, one of the anterior cutaneous branches of the femoral nerve, wrapping into the posterior view.

questions.prompt: Posterior thigh from the gluteal fold to the popliteal fossa (posterior view)
options: Anterior Cutaneous Branches of Femoral Nerve

questions.prompt: Lateral aspect of the upper calf (posterior view)
options: Medial Calcaneal Branches of Tibial Nerve

questions.prompt: Anterolateral side of the lower leg, visible at the lateral edge from behind (posterior view)
options: Medial Calcaneal Branches of Tibial Nerve
questions.explanation: Clinical/older name: superficial peroneal nerve. The posterolateral strip behind the lateral malleolus is sural, not superficial fibular.

questions.prompt: Medial calf below the knee (posterior view)
options: Medial Calcaneal Branches of Tibial Nerve

questions.prompt: Narrow strip over the medial ankle and medial border of the foot (posterior view)
options: Medial Calcaneal Branches of Tibial Nerve

questions.prompt: Posterolateral distal leg and lateral border of the heel and foot (posterior view)
options: Medial Calcaneal Branches of Tibial Nerve

questions.prompt: Skin of the heel, posteromedial (posterior view)
questions.answer: Medial Calcaneal Branches of Tibial Nerve
options: Medial Calcaneal Branches of Tibial Nerve
questions.explanation: Heel skin is supplied by the medial calcaneal branches of the tibial nerve; the lateral edge of the heel gets a sural (lateral calcaneal) contribution.

questions.prompt: Plantar midfoot, forefoot and toes, excluding the heel (plantar view)
questions.explanation: The medial and lateral plantar nerves are the terminal branches of the tibial nerve and supply most plantar skin; the heel itself has separate medial calcaneal supply.
